title: Showmob artifact status board: draft, in PR, published
summary: Where every artifact stands in the pipeline, and what moves it to the next column.

blocks.title: The pipeline, three columns
blocks.body: Showmob has four artifact lifecycle states: draft, preview, published and archived. PR state is a separate workflow dimension. This fictional board is a static snapshot, not a live connection to GitHub. Merging preview content does not publish it.

blocks.heading: Status board (example snapshot)
blocks.caption: Invented counts. Published pages are listed; preview pages stay unlisted but remain viewable by direct link. The /grading index and grade data are passcode-gated. Archived pages never render.

blocks.heading: How to read the board at a glance
blocks.body: Track lifecycle and PR state separately. A merged artifact can remain preview; a published artifact can have an open revision PR. Queue age and blockers indicate review pressure more reliably than an unexplained count.

items.label: Sweep the PR column
items.detail: Review content and checks before deciding whether to merge. Green CI establishes technical gates, not publication approval.

items.label: Check preview pages are not linked publicly
items.detail: Check the actual production catalog and grading route; status is not a substitute for access control.

items.label: Promote deliberately
items.detail: Preview to published is a human call, per artifact, after it has been read like a reader.

blocks.title: Two columns of metadata, two different questions
blocks.body: Lifecycle answers whether the artifact is ready for its audience. PR state answers whether a proposed repository change is under review or merged. The source code defines the lifecycle; a PR badge does not replace it.
